questions.question: Which of the following represents the classic "4 Ts" differential diagnosis for a mass in the anterior mediastinum?
choices: Thymoma, Tracheal mass, Thyroid, T-cell Leukemia
Terrible Lymphoma, Tracheal mass, Thymoma, Thyroid
questions.detail: This is a classic mnemonic for anterior mediastinal masses.

questions.question: A 40-year-old female with drooping eyelids and muscle weakness (Myasthenia Gravis) is found to have an anterior mediastinal mass. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.detail: Approximately 15% of patients with Myasthenia Gravis have a thymoma, and about 30–50% of patients with a thymoma have MG.

questions.question: Which anterior mediastinal mass is most likely to contain fat, fluid, and calcification (the "triple-tissue" sign) on CT?
questions.detail: Teratomas are germ cell tumors that frequently contain multiple tissue densities including fat and bone-like calcifications.

questions.question: A mediastinal mass is identified that demonstrates intense uptake on an I-131 scan. This is diagnostic for:
questions.detail: Ectopic or substernal thyroid tissue will typically take up iodine radiotracers. Conversely, iodine-resistant thyroid cancer may require FDG-PET/CT for staging.

questions.question: Which type of mediastinal mass is most common in the posterior mediastinum and often arises from the sympathetic chain?
questions.detail: Posterior mediastinal masses are predominantly neurogenic in origin.

questions.question: A "water-bottle" shaped heart and widening of the mediastinum on a frontal radiograph should raise suspicion for:
questions.detail: Massive effusions cause the cardiac silhouette to enlarge symmetrically in a "water-bottle" configuration.

questions.question: On CT, a well-circumscribed, low-attenuation (near water density) mass is seen in the right cardiophrenic angle. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.detail: Pericardial cysts are most commonly found in the right cardiophrenic angle and have simple fluid attenuation.

questions.question: Which anatomical landmark marks the boundary between the anterior and middle mediastinum in most classification systems?
choices: The anterior border of the trachea and the posterior heart border
questions.detail: This boundary defines the middle mediastinum, which contains the heart, great vessels, and trachea.

questions.question: Widening of the paratracheal stripe (normal <4 mm) is a common radiographic sign of:
questions.detail: The paratracheal stripe is sensitive to the presence of enlarged nodes or masses in the paratracheal region.

questions.question: A "dumbbell-shaped" mass extending through a neural foramen in the posterior mediastinum is characteristic of:
questions.detail: These tumors often follow the path of spinal nerves through the exit foramina.

questions.question: Which mediastinal compartment contains the esophagus, descending aorta, and the thoracic duct?
questions.detail: In most three-compartment models, these structures are located posteriorly.

questions.question: The presence of air within the mediastinal tissues (pneumomediastinum) in a neonate can lift the thymus, creating the:
questions.detail: Air under the thymic lobes is a hallmark of neonatal pneumomediastinum.

questions.question: Which mediastinal mass is frequently associated with serum elevations of Beta-hCG and Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)?
questions.detail: These biomarkers are used to identify and follow malignant germ cell tumors in the mediastinum.

questions.question: A highly FDG-avid mass in the mediastinum of a 20-year-old with drenching night sweats is most likely:
questions.detail: Lymphoma is a common cause of bulky, hypermetabolic anterior or middle mediastinal masses in young adults.

questions.question: "Extramedullary hematopoiesis" typically presents as:
choices: Anterior mediastinal masses in patients with leukemia
Smooth, lobulated paraspinal masses in patients with chronic anemia
A solitary mass in the middle mediastinum
questions.detail: This is a compensatory mechanism for bone marrow failure/anemia and favors the posterior paraspinal regions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic cause of a "middle mediastinal" cystic mass?
questions.detail: Bronchogenic cysts are congenital foregut malformations typically found near the carina in the middle mediastinum.

questions.question: Dilation of the azygos vein (normal <10 mm on upright film) can be a secondary sign of:
questions.detail: The azygos vein dilates when it must carry an increased volume of venous return.

questions.question: A "lying down adrenal" on neonatal imaging may be a clue to:
questions.detail: In the absence of a kidney, the adrenal gland loses its normal triangular shape and lies flat along the psoas muscle.
